Prepared 15 Nov 2026 · Evidence snapshot 12 Nov 2026 · Report research-2026-11-12.1 · Evidence research-2026-11-11.candidate.1

Evidence & scope

All six retained complete primary texts were actually read: About, Crowd, Home, the photo/video face-recognition collection case, Terms/Privacy index, and worker Data Security. They explicitly offer commercial custom human-generated/validated AI training data with paid freelance microtasks, demographic filtering, general/project tests and training, work-result evaluation, quality-management checking and API delivery. The case reports an anonymous international software customer and provider-reported photo/video totals and workflows; no independent buyer confirmation, performance benefit or corpus payload was inspected. Home/About explicitly describe Clickworker as an LXT subsidiary/group member and 2025 operating transition to clickworker Germany GmbH. Retain Clickworker as its mandatory brand/legal-operating record but propose canonical group org.lxt, already present; no new qualifying supplier group increment. The Terms index names jurisdiction-specific counterparties and links client/worker agreements, but the linked agreements and executed consent/IP/reuse grants were not read. The worker Data Security page says clients use project data for agreed purposes; no blanket rights or operational compliance conclusion follows. Conflicting eight-million and ten-million pool figures remain provider-claimed, not active workers or employees. Exact five already-three-role-passed own-subject assertions retain their original wording/digests; only scoped metadata admission is proposed for separate independent acceptance. No full research/catalog/case-study function closure is claimed. Coordinator independently accepted the stated text/page/visual scopes and group identity. Retained operating-brand organization records are intentionally not counted as additional supplier groups.
